findings.title: SQL injection (error-based) via q
findings.description: Sending a quote in 'q' produced a database error (SQLite) in the response, which means the input is being placed into a SQL query unsafely. This can allow reading or altering database contents.
findings.remediation: Use parameterised queries / prepared statements (never build SQL by string concatenation), and don't return raw database errors to the client.
findings.evidence: SQLite error signature in response: SQLITE_ERROR

findings.title: SQL injection (error-based) via email
findings.description: Sending a quote in 'email' produced a database error (ORM/driver stack trace) in the response, which means the input is being placed into a SQL query unsafely. This can allow reading or altering database contents.
findings.remediation: Use parameterised queries / prepared statements (never build SQL by string concatenation), and don't return raw database errors to the client.
findings.evidence: ORM/driver stack trace error signature in response: sequelize/lib/dialects/sqlite/query.js

findings.title: Content-Security-Policy header missing
findings.description: Without a CSP the browser will run any script that ends up in the page, so a single XSS bug gives an attacker full control. CSP is the main defence-in-depth layer against XSS.
findings.remediation: Add a Content-Security-Policy, starting with something like "default-src 'self'; object-src 'none'; frame-ancestors 'self'" and tightening from there.

findings.title: Referrer-Policy header missing
findings.description: Without an explicit policy the full URL (which may contain tokens, IDs or search terms) can be sent to third-party sites in the Referer header. Modern browsers default to a safer policy, which is why this is LOW.

findings.title: robots.txt lists disallowed paths
findings.description: robots.txt only asks well-behaved crawlers to stay away; it does not protect anything. These paths are worth reviewing manually to make sure they require authentication.
findings.remediation: Never rely on robots.txt to hide sensitive content; protect it with access control.

findings.title: Page served over plain HTTP
findings.description: Traffic is unencrypted, so anyone on the network path can read or modify it. HSTS cannot be applied to plain-HTTP responses.
findings.remediation: Serve the site only over HTTPS and redirect HTTP to HTTPS.
